config.title: Toggle Visibility

intro.title: Toggle Visibility
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that can show or hide a piece of text with the click of a button. You'll learn the core concept of state management using the useState hook to control visibility. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and JSX for structuring your component. By the end, you'll understand how to conditionally render content and handle user interactions in a React application.
intro.usecase: The toggle visibility pattern is fundamental to creating intuitive, space-efficient interfaces across modern web applications. Developers implement this pattern in dashboard controls where users expand/collapse detailed panels, in e-commerce sites with filter sections that hide/show options, and in navigation menus that slide open on mobile devices. This technique allows users to focus on relevant content while keeping secondary information accessible, improving both user experience and interface organization. Mastering visibility toggles is essential for building responsive, clean interfaces that adapt to user needs without overwhelming them with information.

objectives: Initialize a boolean state variable to control visibility in a React component
Implement a click handler function that toggles the boolean state value
Bind the click handler to a button element's onClick event
Render UI elements conditionally based on the boolean state value
Configure a button's text to dynamically update based on the current visibility state
Control the visibility of a text element using conditional rendering techniques
Integrate state management, event handling, and conditional rendering to create a complete toggle visibility feature

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing modules
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported React and the useState hook, which are needed to create a component and manage state for toggling visibility.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ToggleVisibility that returns a JSX element. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component that returns a JSX element like a div or fragment. The component name must match exactly.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ToggleVisibility component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ToggleVisibility is defined and returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: The component is named ToggleVisibility, uses proper TypeScript syntax, and returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly ToggleVisibility and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and ensure it returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize the visibility state
steps.instruction: Inside the ToggleVisibility component, call useState to create a boolean state variable named isVisible with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to destructure the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing a boolean state
const [isActive, setIsActive] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable isVisible initialized to false, ready to control visibility.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with false as the initial value, and the state variable is named isVisible.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useState with false and naming the variable isVisible.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using useState correctly with the proper initial value and variable name.

steps.title: Define the toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your ToggleVisibility component, create a function named toggleVisibility that toggles the isVisible state value.
steps.hint: Use the setter function from useState to update the state. You can toggle a boolean by setting it to the opposite of its current value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleVisibility function is defined that toggles the isVisible state between true and false.
successCriteria: The toggleVisibility function is defined and uses setIsVisible to toggle the boolean state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it properly toggles the isVisible state. Use setIsVisible to update the state to the opposite of its current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function is not defined correctly. Create a function named toggleVisibility that toggles the isVisible state value.

steps.title: Add the main container div
steps.instruction: In your ToggleVisibility component, replace the current return statement with a JSX div element that will serve as the main container for your UI.
steps.hint: Return a <div> element from your component. This will be the root element that holds all other UI elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX div element instead of null, creating the main container structure for the toggle visibility UI.
successCriteria: The ToggleVisibility component returns a <div> element as its JSX output.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a <div> element from the component instead of null.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The component should return a JSX div element. Check that you've replaced 'return null;' with 'return
;' or similar syntax.

steps.title: Add the toggle button
steps.instruction: Inside the container div in your component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Toggle Visibility'.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with the text content 'Toggle Visibility' inside the existing div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with the text 'Toggle Visibility' appears inside the container div.
successCriteria: The button element with text 'Toggle Visibility' is added inside the container div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure the text says exactly 'Toggle Visibility' and it's inside the container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element with the correct text is not present inside the container div.

steps.title: Wire the button click to the handler
steps.instruction: Add an onClick handler to the button that calls the toggleVisibility function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on the button element and set it to the toggleVisibility function reference.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding an event handler to a button
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have an onClick handler that triggers the toggleVisibility function when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element includes an onClick attribute set to the toggleVisibility function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the onClick attribute is set to the toggleVisibility function (without parentheses).
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still needs an onClick handler. Add onClick={toggleVisibility} to the button element.

steps.title: Add conditional content paragraph
steps.instruction: After the button, add a paragraph element that displays 'Now you see me!' only when isVisible is true. Use conditional rendering with a logical AND (&&) operator.
steps.hint:
You can conditionally render JSX by writing {isVisible &&

Now you see me!

}. This will show the paragraph only when isVisible is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The paragraph 'Now you see me!' appears only when the toggle button has been clicked to show content.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'Now you see me!' is conditionally rendered using isVisible state with the && operator.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the && operator to conditionally render the paragraph based on isVisible.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should only appear when isVisible is true. Try using conditional rendering with the && operator.

steps.title: Add status indicator text
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the button that displays the current visibility status. The paragraph should show text like 'Visibility: false' or 'Visibility: true' based on the isVisible state.
steps.hint:
Inside the return statement, add a

tag after the button. Use curly braces to embed the isVisible state value in the paragraph text.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show a paragraph that updates to reflect the current boolean value of isVisible when the button is clicked.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added that displays the current isVisible state value (e.g., 'Visibility: false' or 'Visibility: true').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the actual isVisible value using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph displaying the current visibility state is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Export the ToggleVisibility component as the default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Add the export statement at the end of your file, after the component definition.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: exporting a named component
export default ToggleVisibility;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component is exported and ready to be imported elsewhere.
successCriteria: ToggleVisibility is exported as the default export
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're exporting the ToggleVisibility component as the default export.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component is not exported correctly. Add 'export default ToggleVisibility;' at the end of the file.
